myoglobin.name: Myoglobin
myoglobin.what: Myoglobin is a muscle protein released into blood when muscle — including heart muscle — is damaged.
myoglobin.significance: It rises earliest after myocardial injury but has low cardiac specificity; used as an early marker in multi-marker panels.
myoglobin.limitations: Low cardiac specificity — use in panels with troponin.

faq.a: No — it is an early but non-specific marker; use with troponin.

ck-mb.name: CK-MB (Creatine Kinase-MB)
ck-mb.what: CK-MB is a cardiac-specific isoenzyme of creatine kinase, released when heart muscle is injured.
ck-mb.significance: A classic cardiac marker, largely superseded by troponin but still used in some protocols.
ck-mb.limitations: Largely superseded by troponin; interpret with other markers.

faq.a: Largely superseded by troponin but retained in cardiac panels as an adjunct.

references: Thygesen K et al. Fourth universal definition of myocardial infarction. Eur Heart J. 2019;40(3):237-269.

h-fabp.name: H-FABP (Heart Fatty Acid-Binding Protein)
h-fabp.what: H-FABP is a small cytoplasmic protein abundant in heart muscle, released early after myocardial injury.
h-fabp.significance: Used as an early cardiac marker in some panels, alongside troponin.
h-fabp.limitations: Used as an early marker alongside troponin; not standalone.

faq.a: An early cardiac marker used alongside troponin; not standalone.

references: Clinical guidance on early cardiac markers.

cea.name: CEA (Carcinoembryonic Antigen)
cea.what: CEA is a glycoprotein normally produced during fetal development; levels rise in some cancers, especially colorectal cancer.
cea.significance: Used in colorectal cancer monitoring and, with other markers, screening support.
cea.limitations: Rises in benign conditions and smokers; not diagnostic alone.

faq.q: Is elevated CEA diagnostic of cancer?
faq.a: No — it rises in benign conditions and smoking; use for monitoring with imaging.

hba1c.name: HbA1c (Glycated Hemoglobin)
hba1c.what: HbA1c is hemoglobin with glucose attached, reflecting average blood glucose over the preceding 2–3 months.
hba1c.significance: The standard marker for diabetes diagnosis and long-term glucose control monitoring.
hba1c.interpretation: Reflects average glucose over ~2–3 months; % used for diabetes diagnosis/control.
hba1c.limitations: Affected by hemoglobin variants and anemia.

faq.a: Below ~5.7% is normal; ≥6.5% supports a diabetes diagnosis (varies by guideline).

references: ADA / WHO. Diagnostic criteria for diabetes.

vitamin-d.name: Vitamin D (25-OH)
vitamin-d.what: 25-hydroxyvitamin D is the main circulating form of vitamin D, reflecting body stores.
vitamin-d.significance: Used to screen for vitamin D deficiency.
vitamin-d.limitations: Screening aid; confirm borderline results quantitatively.

faq.q: What does low vitamin D mean?
faq.a: Deficiency or insufficiency; confirm borderline results quantitatively.

references: Clinical guidance on vitamin D testing.

tsh.name: TSH (Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone)
tsh.what: TSH is a pituitary hormone that controls thyroid hormone production; it is the first-line thyroid function test.
tsh.significance: Abnormal TSH indicates hypothyroidism (high TSH) or hyperthyroidism (low TSH).
tsh.interpretation: High = hypothyroid; low = hyperthyroid (first-line thyroid test).
tsh.limitations: Interpret with free T4 and clinical context.

faq.q: What does a high TSH mean?
faq.a: Typically hypothyroidism; low TSH suggests hyperthyroidism — interpret with free T4.

ferritin.name: Ferritin
ferritin.what: Ferritin is the body's iron-storage protein; low ferritin indicates depleted iron stores.
ferritin.significance: The most useful marker for iron-deficiency anemia diagnosis.
ferritin.limitations: Also an acute-phase reactant — can rise in inflammation.

calprotectin.name: Calprotectin
calprotectin.what: Calprotectin is a protein released by white blood cells in the gut during inflammation.
calprotectin.significance: Fecal calprotectin distinguishes inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) from functional disorders (IBS).
calprotectin.interpretation: Elevated = gut inflammation (supports IBD over IBS).
calprotectin.limitations: Supports, not diagnoses; endoscopy is confirmatory.

saa.name: SAA (Serum Amyloid A)
saa.what: Serum amyloid A is an acute-phase protein that rises rapidly during inflammation and infection.
saa.significance: Used alongside CRP for infection/inflammation triage.

faq.a: An acute-phase marker of inflammation/infection, used alongside CRP.
